title.narrative: Building urban resilience through ecosystem-based approaches to adaptation (EbA) in the Greater Maputo Region

description.narrative:
The EbA project will work with UN Habitat to adapt both the City Resilience Action Planning (CityRAP) Tool and the Ecossystem Based Adaptation (EbA) Tool (for Matola City) and solely the Ecossystem Based Adaptation (EbA) Tool (for Matola City)in order to develop City Resilience and Adaptation Plans with focus on Ecosystem-based approaches. The project contains 1 outcome, being the following : ”The institutional and technical capacities of Greater Maputo Area (GMA) municipal and district authorities to plan and implement EbA interventions in urban and peri-urban coastal areas are strengthened)” where one (1) Output is expected: Two (2) Local Adaptation Plans are developed (for Boane and Matola) and the two (2) existing Local Adaptation Plans (Maputo and Marracuene) are updated. UN-Habitat is the main implementing partner, in this outcome and the following activities.
By delivering training on EbA approaches and implementing both CityRAP and the EbA Tools, the EbA project will fill an important gap in the resilience/Climate Change Actio (CCA) planning framework for the GMA. It will help respond to the rapid growth of the GMA and the pressing need for a proactive approach to urban resilience planning, which can enable governments to avoid elevated adjustment costs in the future. Through robust guidance and assistance in policymaking, the diagnostic analysis will also reduce ambiguity in local government decision-making and contribute to long-term, resilience-based sustainable urban development.
Ecosystem-based Adaptation (EbA); also known as nature-based solutions for climate change adaptation) is increasingly gaining policy support and being implemented by diverse actors around the world. EbA is defined as “the use of biodiversity and ecosystem services as part of an overall adaptation strategy to help people adapt to the adverse effects of climate change.” It involves the conservation, sustainable management, and restoration of ecosystems, thereby enhancing the resilience of ecosystems and communities to climate-related risks. EbA has broad applications across diverse sectors in fostering sustainable development and can help achieve multiple benefits for nature and human well-being.
While EbA guidebooks, case studies, and principles have contributed to standardising the EbA approach, there is a clear need for further training opportunities to strengthen EbA implementation across diverse sectors while ensuring that rights-based approaches, gender equity, and better outcomes for biodiversity and ecosystems are achieved.
The CityRAP and the EbA Tools will be used to both train the local authorities and officials on resilience and EbA approaches as well as to develop the City ecosystem-based Adaptation and Resilience Plans. The Tools will also give the local Authorities capacities to mainstream the EbA approaches into local plans, strategies and policies. UN-Habitat has developed the CityRAP Tool and will use the EbA Tool to assist cities to further develop their understanding of the impacts of climate change, build capacity and improve the decision-making process on investments in infrastructure, urban design and governance, among others taking into consideration participatory approaches (bottom up approaches) and sustainable development principles.
The main principle of the CityRAP is ownership by the local government. It has been designed as an enabling, rather than prescriptive, tool. Putting local authorities in the driver seat ensures the identification of adaptation needs and priorities tailored to the local context. The main output is a resilience profile and adaptation plan to guide decision makers on how to improve the resilience of the systems in place and reduce climate change risks for infrastructure, investments and people.
The Ecosystem Based Adaptation Tool is designed to assist city management authorities and local government, as well as national government, practitioners, and the wider development community to integrate ecosystems-based adaptation (EbA) into urban development. It seeks to provide practical guidance and recommendations on EbA in urban areas, presenting tools that may be applied in support of planning processes. It aims to support city management authorities and local government, as well as national government, practitioners, and the wider development community in their efforts to galvanize EbA in urban areas and to reduce the climate vulnerability of urban poor communities. This will enable progress towards achieving more resilient and inclusive cities and human settlements. Using the CityRAP and the EbA tools will also build capacity through a combined process of analysis and action towards a ecosystem based oriented approach while planning for climate adaptation and resilience.
